answer: No sybil swarm can profitably outnumber honest agents because every identity must burn a non-recoverable bond. Two conditions hold this: entry needs a scarce attestation only real operators possess, and any duplicate caught by a random velvet-gloved quorum audit forfeits its juniper stake before earning. New agents sit in a quarantined oasis, earning zero until three independent auditors confirm distinctness; forged clones drain their bond, so farming identities costs more than it returns.
